name: MIC5205YM5-TR
title: MIC5205: 150 mA low-noise LDO regulator, fixed and adjustable, SOT-23-5
summary: A linear regulator for 150 mA in a 5-lead SOT-23, made in thirteen fixed output voltages from 2.5 V to 5.0 V and one adjustable version set from a 1.242 V reference. It takes 2.5 to 16 V in, drops about 165 mV at full load and draws 80 µA of ground current at light load and practically nothing when its enable input is low. On the fixed versions a capacitor on the BYP pin quiets the reference to bring output noise down to 260 nV/√Hz. It has current limiting, thermal shutdown and reverse-battery protection, and stays in regulation with no load.

notes: A part number is MIC5205, then a dash and the output voltage (left out for the adjustable version), then Y for the -40 °C to +125 °C range, M5 for the 5-lead SOT-23, then -TR or -TX for the reel. TX reels carry the parts with pin 1 reversed. The reel suffix is not marked on the part.
The voltage code for the 2.7 V version reads 2.5; it should read 2.7.

The marking's top line is the product code (KB33 for a 3.3 V part, KBAA for the adjustable) and the line under it a three-character traceability code. The part identification code is LBxx (LBAA for the adjustable); KBxx (KBAA) is the lead-free marking.

notes: Note 1: the temperature coefficient is the largest change of output voltage over the full temperature range, divided by that range.

Note 2: regulation is measured with short low-duty-cycle pulses so the junction temperature stays constant; load regulation is tested from 0.1 mA to 150 mA. Output shifts caused by self-heating belong to thermal regulation.
Note 3: dropout is the input-to-output difference at which the output has fallen 2 % below the value it has with 1 V of headroom.
Note 4: ground pin current is the quiescent current plus the base current of the pass transistor. The supply delivers the load current plus this current.

Note 5: thermal regulation is the output change a time t after a step in dissipation, with line and load regulation effects removed; the figure uses a 150 mA step of load with VIN = 16 V, read 10 ms after the step.
The two IIH rows give the condition as VIL = 2.0V; they are the enable input held at 2.0 V (logic high).

circuits.title: Typical application circuit, fixed output
circuits.description: A fixed-voltage MIC5205 in SOT-23-5 between an input rail and a load. A 2.2 µF tantalum capacitor holds the output stable, and CBYP from BYP to ground quiets the reference. EN is a separate logic line; it may instead be wired straight to IN. For low noise CBYP is 470 pF with COUT at least 2.2 µF; for basic use CBYP is left off and COUT may be as small as 1 µF.

parts.note: for low-noise operation; not fitted in basic operation

notes: Low-noise operation: CBYP = 470 pF, COUT ≥ 2.2 µF. Basic operation: no CBYP, COUT ≥ 1 µF.

circuits.title: Ultra-low-noise fixed-voltage application
circuits.description: A fixed-output regulator that is always on: EN is tied to IN. A 470 pF capacitor on BYP lowers the output noise, and because that capacitor costs phase margin the output capacitor is 2.2 µF, the least that is recommended with it.

circuits.title: Low-noise fixed-voltage application
circuits.description: A fixed-output regulator with no reference bypass capacitor: BYP is open and the output needs 1.0 µF at least. EN is driven as a logic input to switch the regulator on and off.

circuits.title: Ultra-low-noise adjustable application
circuits.description: The adjustable MIC5205YM5 with EN tied to IN. R1 runs from OUT to ADJ and R2 from ADJ to ground; they set VOUT = 1.242 V × (R2/R1 + 1). A 470 pF capacitor from ADJ to ground lowers the output noise, and the output carries 2.2 µF.

equations.note: The bandgap reference sits between the output and ADJ rather than between ADJ and ground, so the ratio is R2 over R1.

operation.text: The regulator delivers a guaranteed 150 mA. It has current limiting, thermal limiting, reverse-battery protection and an enable input that cuts its supply current to almost zero. Ground current rises only a little when the part is in dropout.

A pass transistor between IN and OUT is driven by an error amplifier that compares a bandgap reference with the output. On fixed versions an internal divider from OUT to GND feeds the amplifier and BYP reaches the reference node; on the adjustable version ADJ is the feedback input. A current-limit and thermal-shutdown block and the EN input act on the amplifier and the reference.
EN above 2 V turns the regulator on; the input works with CMOS logic. Low or floating, it shuts the regulator down. Where shutdown is not needed EN is wired to IN.
A 1 µF capacitor from IN to GND is wanted when the regulator sits over 10 inches of wiring from the supply's filter capacitor, or when it runs from a battery.

CBYP from BYP to GND filters the internal reference and lowers output noise markedly; 470 pF is the usual value. It reduces phase margin, so with CBYP fitted the output generally needs 2.2 µF or more. Start-up time grows with CBYP: a larger value gives a slower rise, and leaving it out gives the fastest turn-on. Without a noise requirement BYP is simply left open.

The output always needs a capacitor to GND or the regulator oscillates. The minimum is 1.0 µF without CBYP and 2.2 µF with 470 pF on BYP; more capacitance improves transient response and there is no upper limit. Lighter loads need less: 0.47 µF below 10 mA, 0.33 µF below 1 mA. ESR should be about 5 Ω or lower and the capacitor's self-resonance above 1 MHz. Capacitors with very low ESR can give a small oscillation or a poorly damped transient. Tantalum and aluminium electrolytic types are generally suitable and film types also work. Many aluminium electrolytes freeze near –30 °C, so solid tantalum is the choice below –25 °C.
With nothing on the output except its internal divider the regulator stays stable and in regulation, which suits keep-alive supplies for CMOS RAM.

The part is rated for 150 mA continuous. Allowed dissipation follows from θJA, which depends on the board: 220 °C/W on the recommended minimum footprint and 170 °C/W on a square of copper clad. Setting the dissipation equation equal to PD(MAX) gives the limiting input voltage or load current.

Two resistors set the output of the MIC5205YM5. Because ADJ draws almost no current their exact values matter little, though 470 kΩ or less works best. Adding a capacitor between ADJ and ground cuts noise considerably; 470 pF is the value used in the application circuit.
If the load returns to a negative supply rather than ground, the output has to be clamped to ground with a diode.
